The test image shows tomato leaves with numerous small yellow/pale spots scattered across the upper leaf surface, with significant overall leaf yellowing. The spots appear discrete without obvious dark centers or concentric rings. The affected part is the leaf.

Top candidates: Leaf Mold (pale greenish-yellow spots on upper surface), Bacterial Speck (small spots with yellow halos), Septoria Leaf Blotch.

Let me view one reference image for the best candidate — Leaf Mold.

The reference image for Leaf Mold shows yellowish patches on the upper leaf surface, consistent with the description. The test image matches well: numerous discrete pale/yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces with overall leaf yellowing, fitting the Leaf Mold profile of "pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surface" with "indistinct chlorosis."

Bacterial Speck would show small black specks (not visible here), and Septoria would have tan/gray lesions with dark pycnidia. The pattern of scattered yellow spots without dark centers or concentric rings points to Leaf Mold.
